newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 20.42 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 20.42 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 36 basis points to 20.42 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 120 billion bolivars of 177- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 20.78 percent coupon for a price of 100.16 percent. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 20.78 percent

The bank also sold 40 billion bolivars of 266-day notes with a 21.31 percent coupon at a price of 99.08 percent, and 40 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 21.87 percent coupon at an average price of 98.51 percent.
Yields for these notes fell four basis points to 22.77 percent for the 266-day bills, and 84 basis points to 23.72 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
